title: Rasterized candlestick CNN does not beat numeric HAR/GARCH volatility baselines
claim: A lightweight CNN trained on 48x48 rendered 20-day OHLCV candlestick images failed to improve next-week realized variance forecasts versus numeric OHLC/HAR/GARCH baselines across SPY, QQQ, IWM, EEM, GLD, TLT, and SLV.

guardrails: feature date t uses only OHLCV information through t
target uses close-to-close realized variance over t+1 through t+5
support requires at least 4 strict asset wins, CNN as panel best model, and panel DM t < -3

interpretation: For this daily OHLCV volatility task, the raster image representation appears to discard scale and rank information that numeric OHLC/HAR/range features retain. The result is consistent with prior project evidence that simple ML/image encodings often fail to beat disciplined numeric volatility baselines.
limitations: CNN uses coarse RV bucket classification
not a high-frequency image or order-book experiment
